page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a KVM-hypervised GPU server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. This x86_64 architecture CPU provides 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs under a shared allocation model, operating at a base speed of 2.0 GHz. The system features 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier (top 10%) performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU metrics. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512 and AES. Memory performance is mixed; while cached read-only small block bandwidth ranks in the top 25%, the Passmark memory score falls into the average (middle 50%) category.

The dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs provide substantial acceleration for machine learning workloads. LLM inference benchmarks for a small 135M model place both prompt processing and text generation in the top 10% tier. For a medium 7B model, inference speeds remain strong (top 25%). However, scaling to a large 70B model drops prompt processing and text generation performance to the average (middle 50%) tier, indicating a hardware limitation for very large parameter models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high compute and memory density paired with enterprise-grade GPU acceleration, though the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs. This configuration is suited for medium-scale LLM inference, image processing, ray tracing, and database operations, but is less optimal for workloads requiring dedicated CPU pinning or high-capacity local NVMe storage.
